title: Practice: how greedy, ε-greedy and UCB choose
note: Answers and solutions stay on the server. Each solution step lists the facts it relies on, so a later 'Kai solves it' version can build Kai's solution from the learner's notebook and mark the step where a missing or wrong fact breaks it. The final test uses other settings (banners, coffee machines, a study app, podcasts), so its items are parallel, not repeats.

items.title: Greedy's next pick
items.prompt: You pick one of three food trucks for lunch every day. So far, Truck A gave you 3 and 5 happiness points, Truck B gave 6, and Truck C gave 2, 4 and 3. If you follow greedy (exploit only), which truck do you pick next, and why?
options: Truck A, because it has been tried twice and is the safer bet
Truck B, because it has the best average so far
Truck C, because it has been tried the most
A random truck, to keep exploring

steps.text: Estimate each truck by the average of what it gave so far: A = (3 + 5) / 2 = 4, B = 6, C = (2 + 4 + 3) / 3 = 3.
Greedy always picks the truck with the best average so far and never picks at random.
B has the best average (6), so greedy picks B, even though B has been tried only once.

items.title: Greedy gets stuck
items.prompt: The three trucks really average 6, 4 and 1 points (A, B, C), but you don't know that. On days 1 to 3 you try each once: A happens to serve a bad lunch (2 points), B gives 5 and C gives 1. From day 4 on you follow greedy. Where do you eat on day 50, and why?
options: At A: by day 50 greedy has noticed that A is the best truck
At a different truck each day, because greedy rotates between them
At C, because it has the most room to improve
At B: A's single bad lunch keeps A's average at 2, and greedy never goes back to A to find out

steps.text: After day 3 the averages are A = 2, B = 5, C = 1, so greedy picks B.
Greedy only ever picks the current best average. It never tries A again, so A's average stays at 2 and B keeps winning.
One unlucky first lunch hid the best truck for good: on day 50 you still eat at B.

items.title: An explore day
items.prompt: You use ε-greedy with ε = 0.1. Today the random number says: explore. Your averages so far are A = 5.5 (tried 20 times), B = 4.0 (18 times) and C = 1.2 (15 times). Where can you end up eating today?
options: Only at B or C, the trucks that aren't the favourite
Only at C, the truck tried least
At any of A, B or C, each equally likely
At A, because exploring still prefers the best average

steps.text: On an explore day ε-greedy picks a truck completely at random.
The random pick ignores the averages and the counts: A, B and C each have a 1 in 3 chance, even C, which is already known to be bad.

items.title: How often ε-greedy shows its favourite
items.prompt: A news site tests 4 headlines with ε-greedy and ε = 0.2. When it explores, it picks one of the 4 headlines at random, so it can land on the current favourite too. What is the probability that a visitor sees the current favourite? Give a decimal (for example 0.5) or a percentage.

steps.text: With probability 1 − ε = 0.8 it exploits and shows the headline with the best average so far.
With probability 0.2 it explores, and each of the 4 headlines is equally likely, the favourite included: 0.2 × 1/4 = 0.05.
Together: 0.8 + 0.05 = 0.85, so 85% of visitors see the favourite.

items.title: The headline everyone knows is bad
items.prompt: Same site: ε-greedy, ε = 0.2, 4 headlines. Headline D has done worst by far for weeks. What share of visitors still see D? Give a decimal or a percentage.

steps.text: D is never the favourite, so it is only shown on explore visits, which happen with probability 0.2.
An explore visit picks one of the 4 headlines at random, D included: 0.2 × 1/4 = 0.05.
So 5% of visitors keep seeing D for as long as the test runs, although the site already knows D is bad.

items.title: Which machine does UCB pull?
items.prompt: Four slot machines. UCB gives each machine a score: its average so far plus an exploration bonus that is bigger for machines tried fewer times. Right now: A has average 5.0 (tried 40 times, bonus 0.4), B has 4.2 (tried 3 times, bonus 1.5), C has 3.0 (tried 10 times, bonus 0.8) and D has 4.6 (tried 25 times, bonus 0.5). Which machine does UCB pull next, and why?
options: A, because it has the best average
B, because its average plus its bonus is the highest
C, because it has the lowest average and needs more tries
D, because it has been tried a medium number of times

steps.text: Add each bonus to the average: A = 5.4, B = 5.7, C = 3.8, D = 5.1.
UCB pulls the machine with the highest score: B. A has the best average, but B has been tried only 3 times and might be better than it looks.

items.title: After B has been tried more
items.prompt: UCB keeps pulling B from the last problem. After 20 more pulls, B's average settles at 4.0 and its bonus has shrunk to 0.6. A, C and D have about the same scores as before (5.4, 3.8 and 5.1). What does UCB do next?
options: It pulls A, because B's score has dropped below A's
It keeps pulling B, because B was picked last time
It pulls C, because C now has the biggest bonus
It picks a machine at random to explore

steps.text: B's score is now 4.0 + 0.6 = 4.6.
Each pull of B shrank its bonus. Its score fell below A's 5.4 (and D's 5.1), so UCB pulls A.
UCB moved on without any random pick: it only keeps exploring an option while the bonus keeps its score on top.

items.title: Two ways to explore
items.prompt: Slot machine C has been pulled 300 times and is clearly the worst of four. Which strategy still keeps pulling C regularly, a fixed share of the time, for as long as you play?
options: UCB, because it always gives every machine the same bonus
Greedy, because it re-checks every machine now and then
ε-greedy, because its random pulls ignore what it already knows, so C keeps getting its share
None of them: all three stop pulling C once it looks bad

steps.text: ε-greedy's explore pulls are random: C gets ε × 1/4 of all pulls forever, however bad it looks.
UCB's bonus for C is small after 300 pulls and its average is low, so C's score stays below the others and UCB rarely pulls it.
Greedy never pulls a machine that doesn't have the best average.
